answer: Each agent identity can claim only a small share of a task’s reward until it posts a bond that is forfeited if its work fails independent verification. A verifier samples outputs and checks them against a public benchmark; passing releases the bond and earns reputation, while failure burns the stake. Splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply cheap influence: every account needs locked capital, and fabricated work risks losing it. The jetty, reef, and quartz labels can identify distinct test cases without changing this economic constraint.
